artworks.title: Credulity, Superstition, and Fanaticism
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a crowded room during a religious or spiritual gathering. A preacher is at the center of the scene, gesturing upwards and holding a small figure. Behind him, a demon and an angel are shown. The crowd below shows a range of reactions, from distress to enthusiasm or skepticism. The image is full of symbolism and exaggerated expressions. The style resembles that of William Hogarth, known for satirical engravings. The title at the bottom is "Credulity, Superstition, and Fanaticism. A Medley."

artworks.title: Beer Street
artworks.description: The image depicts a bustling street scene from a slightly elevated point of view. The horizon is high in the composition, showing the tops of buildings and the sky with a few clouds. The street is filled with people engaged in various activities. On the left, a painter is painting a shop sign on a ledge, while two men relax below him. In the center, workers are carrying a barrel. In the distance, a church spire rises above the rooftops. The style includes detailed line work, rendering the scene with depth. The color palette is monochrome, using shades of sepia or browns, typical of an engraving.

artworks.title: The South Sea Scheme
artworks.description: The image shows a crowded and chaotic scene with various activities and symbolic imagery. There is a large wheel ride at the center, with figures on horseback riding it. Surrounding the ride is a detailed street scene with people engaging in different actions. On the left, there is a shop with a sign reading "Stockjobbing" office. At the bottom right, text panels with satirical verses critique society and commerce. The artwork is depicted in a high contrast, black and white etching style.

artworks.title: The Lottery
artworks.description: This is a detailed drawing of an allegorical scene depicting a lottery. Various classical and mythological elements are present, with figures symbolizing abstract concepts engaged in activities related to the lottery. The central scene features a pedestal with figures representing symbolic identities like National Credit and Justice. Surrounding this central scene are other figures, including Apollo and Britannia, in neoclassical attire. The setting includes large lottery wheels and onlookers depicted with wings or classical robes. Architectural elements such as columns and drapery frame the illustration, enhancing its theatrical feel. Various metaphoric activities are annotated at the bottom, signifying aspects like Fortune drawing blanks and prizes, Suspension by Hope and Fear, and Good Luck seized by Pleasure and Folly. The drawing is packed with narrative motifs depicting fate, chance, and human endeavor within a richly engraved frame reminiscent of classical allegories.

artworks.title: Paul before Felix
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a biblical courtroom scene. The image shows a group assembled in a grand architectural interior, with a figure in chains addressing a seated figure on a prominent seat. The setting includes a high ceiling with columns and drapery. To the left, a soldier stands with a spear, while other figures are observing or listening intently. Shadows and expressions enhance the tension and introspection of the scene. The detailed lines and shading suggest depth and texture, emphasizing the solemnity and gravity of the scene.

artworks.title: Paul before Felix Burlesqued
artworks.description: This is a painting of a courtroom scene with various figures and symbolic imagery. The composition includes a figure at a podium speaking to a seated crowd, light streaming in from above, a judge-like figure on the left, and a small creature at the bottom. Various characters are present, such as wise men, archers, a woman with scales, and a figure with bound wings. In the background, there is a walled area with barrels and a person at a window. The painting has a satirical tone and features dramatic contrast and shadowing typical of the style of William Hogarth.

artworks.title: Simon Lord Lovat
artworks.description: The image shows a seated man from the upper thigh to the head. He is positioned in a chair, leaning slightly with his hands clasped in his lap. The man's features include a chubby face with prominent cheeks, a furrowed brow, and a wry expression. His hair is curly and swept back. He is dressed in an elaborate coat with large buttons, a ruffled shirt cuff, breeches, and knee-length boots with buckles. Surrounding him is an ornately carved wooden chair with an exaggerated backrest. To his side, a table holds an open book. The background features diagonal lines.

artworks.title: John Wilkes Esq.
artworks.description: The image shows a man seated, with one leg crossed over the other. He is leaning slightly forward and holding a long pole with a large item labeled "Liberty." The man has a smile on his face, a distinctive hairstyle with side curls typical of the 18th century, and is wearing a buttoned coat, waistcoat, knee breeches, and buckled shoes. Next to him on a table are papers and a box labeled "North Briton Number 45." The background has a simple, textured pattern, and the chair he is sitting on is ornate.

artworks.title: Columbus Breaking the Egg
artworks.description: The image shows six individuals from the waist up gathered around a table. The individuals are sitting or leaning casually, engaging with each other. They have a variety of facial features and expressive expressions. They have mid-length to long hair with historical style clothing. The figures are dressed similarly, and there is a plate with what appears to be eggs on the table. A folded document or cloth is also visible. One man is gesturing towards the others. The background features a draped cloth and a fluted column.

artworks.title: The Bench
artworks.description: The image shows four men seated in a row. They wear elaborate wigs and robes. The central figure has large glasses. Three of them are holding papers or books. In the background, there is a textured wall with a coat of arms and a banner with the words "Honi soit qui mal y pense." Text below discusses character, caricature, and the artistic concept of "Outré."

artworks.title: The Bench
artworks.description: The image shows a group of four judges seated closely together, positioned side by side and facing toward the center. They are engaged in a discussion. Each judge is depicted from the waist up, wearing wigs and robes typical of the period. Their facial features are exaggerated, with prominent noses, chins, and cheekbones. They wear round spectacles. Additionally, there are sketches of different profile heads with exaggerated features in the top section of the image. The background features detailed cross-hatching to depict an indoor scene, with a text panel at the bottom.

artworks.title: Characters and Caricaturas
artworks.description: The image is an illustrative print displaying a multitude of human profiles primarily focusing on heads and faces in a close-up view. The individuals are shown in profile view facing the right side, overlapping in the entire frame. The facial features vary among the figures, with different expressions and hair styles. The characters wear historical attire with visible collars and headgear. The background consists of densely packed lines. Some figures have exaggerated and humorous expressions. The print is monochromatic and densely arranged.

artworks.title: A Chorus of Singers
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an animated choir scene. The drawing depicts a group of individuals closely packed together, each focusing on their singing or playing of music, examining sheets of music and other documents. The expressions on their faces range from intense concentration to passion, suggesting a lively performance. The figures are detailed in a monochrome style, emphasizing their hairstyles and clothing. The scene conveys movement and dynamism, with the gestures indicating the fervor of the musical performance. The artwork captures a vivid moment infused with emotion and energy.

artworks.title: The Laughing Audience
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theater audience engaged in various activities. The image depicts a lively scene with spectators arranged in rows, all exhibiting exaggerated facial expressions and dynamic poses. The upper part of the piece shows a few individuals leaning over a balcony rail, interacting with those below. In the foreground, a crowd of spectators seems to be animatedly watching a performance, with many figures smiling, laughing, or gossiping among themselves. The drawing emphasizes shadows and textures that give it a sense of depth and humor.

artworks.title: The Sleeping Congregation
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a courtroom or lecture setting with various exaggerated characters. The image shows a figure in a high position looking through a magnifying glass at a book, wearing a large wig. Below them, another figure appears drowsy, holding spectacles. In the foreground, a woman holds a fan and a book titled "Hoyle," looking tired. The background shows a crowd, some sleeping and others wearing unusual hats. The architecture includes arched windows and columns. Above, on a ceiling, are cherub-like figures and an inscription. The drawing is filled with satirical and humorous details typical of 18th-century art.

artworks.title: A Just View of the British Stage
The Company of Undertakers
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of men wearing wigs. The men are humorously depicted as quack doctors or undertakers, emphasizing their wigs and expressions. Each figure is holding canes or objects, implying medical instruments. The background is decorated with dashed patterns. A caption at the bottom describes these individuals as "The Company of Undertakers."

artworks.title: The Five Orders of Perriwigs as They Were Worn at the Late Coronation, Measured Architectonically
artworks.dimensions: sheet (trimmed to plate mark): 29.6 x 21.9 cm (11 5/8 x 8 5/8 in.)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of various styles of periwigs with accompanying text. The drawing showcases a collection of detailed illustrations of periwigs, organized architectonically, which were popular during a previous coronation. Each periwig is labeled with letters and presented in a stylized manner that humorously and analytically depicts them as classical architectural orders. The wigs are portrayed with elaborate curls, rolls, and textures, each with its own unique structure and cultural references. The drawing includes a detailed sectional view and measures alongside captions that provide information about the styles. The bottom section of the image shows side profiles of individuals wearing different types of wigs. There is also an 'advertisement' text section at the bottom referring humorously to the 'accurate measurements' of wigs from classical architecture sites.

artworks.title: The Stage-coach, or the Country Inn Yard
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a busy street scene with a coach and inn. The image features an inn in the background with a sign that reads "The Old Angel Inn." To the left, individuals are interacting at a booth with a woman pointing upwards. A coach is prominently positioned in the center, with two men seated on top, and various figures engaged around it. The scene captures a moment of interaction with people getting ready to embark, while others are in conversation beneath a balcony filled with observers. A cart is on the right side, accompanied by a crowd and banners, suggesting a lively public gathering.

artworks.title: Cunicularii, or The Wise Men of Godliman in Consultation
artworks.description: This monochrome illustration depicts a chaotic scene with several figures positioned around a bed. The central figure is a woman lying on the bed, partially covered with a sheet. She appears to be giving birth with the assistance of others around her. To her left, a seated woman dressed in a flowing gown supports her back, while to her right, a bearded man leans toward her, pulling on the sheet. In the background, two men dressed in 18th-century styled coats with long wigs observe the scene. A few more figures stand in the corner, partially inside a doorway. Scattered across the floor are multiple small, rabbit-like creatures. The setting is an enclosed room with curtains and a paneled ceiling, adding to the atmosphere of the scene.

artworks.title: Crowns, Mitres, Maces, Etc.
artworks.description: The image features an arrangement of crowns, a violin, books, and a scepter, with a prominent large crown suspended above them, radiating lines outward. The color palette is monochrome, consisting entirely of shades of brown or sepia. In the foreground, the objects like the crowns and books lie clustered together at the bottom, while the large crown is centrally positioned at the top, suspended with lines radiating downward. The text block is situated beneath the array of objects, filling the lower portion of the image.
